claim: The content-addressed storage backend stores each `MergeTree` part file once under a content hash so multiple servers can share a pool without byte duplication or Keeper state proportional to data volume.
The CAS pool protocol has no external coordinator and no ZooKeeper/Keeper usage; `MountLeaseKeeper` is a lease renewer rather than a Keeper client.

The shared CAS data plane is shared-nothing: servers share only the content-addressed `blobs/` space, and correctness requires conditional writes on individual objects rather than a serializable metadata service.
A blob is identified by the pair `BlobHashAlgo` and `BlobDigest`; a bare digest is not an identity because pools may mix `CityHash128`, `XXH3_128`, and `Sha256`.
CAS blob hashing is streaming, and `CityHash128` preserves ClickHouse's legacy chunked `CityHash128WithSeed` convention rather than using a one-shot hash for large inputs.

A stored blob object consists of a 256-byte envelope header followed by its payload; the header carries a fresh random `incarnation_tag` for each upload attempt, while the digest covers only the payload.
The only mutable CAS data is ref state binding a part name to a manifest id; blobs, part manifests, and their metadata are write-once objects.
A blob is live if a live manifest names it, and a manifest is live if a committed or precommitted ref names it.

The backend must provide read-after-write visibility, conditional create via `putIfAbsent`, conditional overwrite via `casPut` or `putOverwrite`, exact-token deletion via `deleteExact`, no versioning or delete markers, and token-to-content stability.
`deleteExact(key, token)` deletes only the named object incarnation; `TokenMismatch` leaves the object readable.
The backend capability probe runs at every writable mount and refuses an object store that does not enforce the CAS conditions.
`Mode::EmulatedSingleProcess` token bookkeeping is per-process and sharing such a pool between processes is not currently enforced against, so this mode can fail silently when misconfigured.
A condemned blob is never adopted or server-side-copied; it is recreated from the writer's own source bytes under a fresh `incarnation_tag`.
The durable part-write order is `stageManifest` → `precommitAdd` → `putBlob` → `promote`, and adopting an existing blob is legal only after this build's precommit is durable.
Every destructive CAS operation names the exact incarnation token it intends to remove.
CAS has exactly one blob-body deletion site: the pre-CAS `pending_deletes` phase of a GC round, limited to entries marked `delete_pending` by a previously published round.
GC never invents a ref transition; abandoned precommit cleanup is performed by the writer or its successor rather than by a synthetic GC event.

CAS failure handling is conservative: lost folds, stale snapshots, duplicated records, and crashed leaders can only postpone reclamation because in-degree is an idempotent set of source edges rather than a counter.

The CAS safety triad is no-dangle, no-loss, and no-return: live references resolve through present keys, deletion requires durable retirement and later zero reachability with the exact token, and a retired `(kind, hash, token)` cannot become a valid dependency again.
`PartWriteTxn` is in-memory only and is never resumed after restart; a dead precommit is removed rather than promoted.
Promotion fails closed when a leaf is neither token-protected nor backed by a durable manifest edge.
A precommit may name only a manifest minted by the transaction or the ref's current committed manifest; granting fresh ownership to a foreign manifest id is rejected to prevent ABA reuse.
Publishing over an existing ref binding throws; an intentional repoint must use `republishRef`.
An operation with an uncertain conditional-write outcome is treated as `PrecommitState::Uncertain`, which behaves as `NotAttempted` for admission and as `Durable` for cleanup.
Every durable write or delete captures the mount fence generation at admission and rechecks it immediately before the object-store call and on every conditional retry; reads are not fence-gated.
The append-mode `writeFile` path is safe only under the single-appender invariant: it freezes the carried prefix when opened and its CAS loop re-reads the token but not the base content.
A `ManifestRef` has at most one owner in a table, in either the `Committed` or `Precommit` slot.
`writer_epoch` is durable-monotone and never reissued, and every re-materialization of a fixed `(namespace, shard)` carries a strictly greater incarnation to close ABA.
A transaction never publishes a ref before `commit`; its destructor abandons open builds.
The GC condemnation marker is add-only: GC may change `Clean` to `Condemned` and delete the marker after a confirmed body delete, but never changes `Condemned` back to `Clean`.
CAS crash safety is intentionally asymmetric: every crash point may leak objects, but no crash point loses acknowledged data or creates a dangling reference.
The former `RefSidecar` and mutable-per-part-file classification are deleted; `uuid.txt`, `txn_version.txt`, and `metadata_version.txt` are ordinary manifest entries.
A small part file is stored inline in the manifest when its size is at most 1 MiB; larger files spill to a blob, and `primary.idx` plus `.bin`, `.mrk*`, and `.cmrk*` files are blob-class candidates.
A byte-equal repoint performs zero pool mutations, including no manifest PUT and no ref-log record.
Namespace files under `roots/<srid>/<ns>/_files/<name>` and loose mountpoint objects under `roots/<srid>/<path>` bypass CAS and are removed eagerly because they are not shared.
The `@cas@` suffix on a table-directory segment is the boundary: nodes inside it are content-addressed and immutable, while nodes outside it are verbatim.

The CAS design rejects a Merkle `treeId` layer, EBR or epoch-based GC, integer refcounts, `gc/registry` as discovery authority, endpoint-plus-prefix pool matching, and CAS-specific fields in `ReplicatedMergeTreePartHeader`.
Blob bodies use keys shaped as `blobs/<algo>/<hex[0:2]>/<hex>`, while `gc_shards` is a separate GC reduction fan-out routed by the high 64 bits of the digest.
The `gc_shards` setting is fixed at pool creation and must be at least 1; it is not the same as the first-two-hex-digit S3 key sharding.
CAS metadata objects use a text envelope whose header is `{"type":"cas_<object>","v":N}`; `.zst` keys denote kinds whose policy always compresses.
`putIfAbsent` precondition failure is an outcome rather than an exception, while a wrong-dialect token is rejected locally before a conditional overwrite reaches the wire.
A blob `.meta` sidecar has only `Clean` and `Condemned` states; an absent sidecar reads as `Clean`, and the sidecar contains no token.
`dedup_head_first_min_bytes` defaults to 1 MiB; below that threshold a speculative conditional PUT is preferred to a HEAD plus PUT unless the dedup cache already says the blob is present.

A blob upload retries at most 8 times, mints a fresh `incarnation_tag` per attempt, verifies the source byte count, and throws retry-later without acknowledging anything when the outcome remains unresolved.

When two writers upload identical content, one `If-None-Match: *` request succeeds and the other receives 412, HEADs the object, reads `.meta`, and adopts the winner's token after its own precommit edge is durable.

A writer that adopts a blob token must have observed a non-`Condemned` marker after its precommit edge became durable, so the next GC fold can spare the blob; a resurrection changes the token and makes a stale `deleteExact` return `TokenMismatch`.
The `server_root_id` setting is required, immutable, and validated without sanitizing fallback; it roots `gc/server-roots/<srid>/`, `roots/<srid>/`, `cas/manifests/<srid>/`, and `staging/<srid>/`.
The server-root owner object is never deleted or reassigned; it binds `server_root_id` to one `server_uuid`, and an absent owner over a non-empty owned subtree fails with `CORRUPTED_DATA`.
The object `gc/server-roots/<srid>/mount` carries both the liveness lease and build watermark, including `writer_epoch`, renewal `seq`, `expires_at_ms`, `min_active`, and `gc_fenced`.
The default mount lease cadence is `mount_renew_period` 10 seconds with `mount_lease_ttl_ms` 30 seconds, and renewal uses token-guarded `putOverwrite` with `seq + 1`.
The local mount fence uses `CLOCK_BOOTTIME`, not `CLOCK_MONOTONIC`, so a VM resumed from suspend observes the elapsed lease deadline.
GC classifies a mount with `gc_fenced` as already fenced and a mount with `min_active == UINT64_MAX` as cleanly terminated; fencing preserves the body and uses token-guarded `putOverwrite`.
`writer_epoch` is durably monotone, while `build_sequence` resets on process start; global ordering is the lexicographic pair `(writer_epoch, build_sequence)`.
The mount lifecycle writes a terminal farewell with `min_active = UINT64_MAX` only after a certified drain; if the drain is not certified, no farewell is written.
A part manifest contains `ref`, `root_namespace_id`, `payload_digest`, and strictly path-sorted `entries`; `payload_digest` is integrity/debug metadata rather than a key or GC edge.
A manifest id is `ManifestRef = {writer_epoch, build_sequence, manifest_ordinal}` and is not a content hash or random value.
A pre-precommit orphan manifest has no ref-log owner edge and is reclaimed by the orphan sweep, whereas a dangling precommit must first have its binding removed before GC can reclaim the body.
Blob liveness is represented by a set of source edges; `precommitAdd` creates `+1` edges, owner removals create `-1` edges, `promote` creates no edge, and inline manifest entries create none.
`CasManifestReader` keys its decode cache by `(ManifestId, Token)` and performs a mandatory HEAD even on a cache hit to prove existence and obtain the token.
Ref transaction ids are per-namespace contiguous pairs `(writer_epoch, ref_sequence)` rendered as fixed-width hexadecimal fields; `applyRefLogTxn` rejects a non-successor id with `CORRUPTED_DATA`.
The ref lane has no append-to-object or CAS-swapped mutable pointer: ref logs and snapshots are immutable objects created with conditional creates, and only GC deletes ref objects.

The implemented ref lane trusts a cold LIST as complete and enforces strict increase but not middle-log contiguity, so a missing middle log can be silently skipped; the v9 contiguous-chain design exists only in TLA+ models and plans.
GC discovers the ref live set by listing `cas/ns/stream/`, joining opaque life ids to one catalog cut, and folding each admitted log only after its complete coverage is durable.
The canonical part publication sequence is `stageManifest` → `precommitAdd` → `putBlob` → `promote`; `promote` publishes no blob deltas because the manifest retains an owner.
Relink promotion is authorized only by literal `yes`; missing, unknown, timeout, and transport-error outcomes are locally generated `NETWORK_ERROR` retry outcomes rather than byte-fetch success.
A confirmed relink is not proven dangle-free when a listing page is incomplete; `CaRelinkConfirmCore.tla` produces a counterexample and `ca-fsck` is the backstop.
The implemented GC round is a single pass of 18 named phases ending in exactly one `gc/state` CAS; the older `fold → retire → fence → recheck → trim` shape is superseded.

The GC lease is work de-duplication rather than mutual exclusion: one `gc/state` CAS adopts a round, attempt-scoped artifacts isolate leaders, pre-CAS destructive work uses published state, and exact-token deletes protect newer incarnations.

GC computes `suppress_destructive` once from anomalies, carried holds, and incomplete frontiers, and threads it through merge, ref cleanup, and namespace janitor so destructive decisions cannot diverge.

`gc/state` is the durable round-adoption state and exactly one CAS per round publishes it; the fold seal records generation, parent generation, catalog-life coverage, source-edge runs, and condemned summaries.
Condemned entries are stored as sentinel rows in the source-edge run; there is no separate retired-list object and no run-file list outside the fold seal.

A blob candidate is HEAD-observed with an exact token when its edge set becomes empty; a carried candidate pays no HEAD, and missing bodies are non-throwing while present-but-invalid bodies are `CORRUPTED_DATA`.

A condemned entry graduates only after surviving the required round delay and confirmed `Condemned` evidence for the exact `(hash, token)`; recovery spares it, and a token mismatch leaves the newer blob untouched.

The GC coordinator owns discovery, round visibility, the global fence, and generation advancement; reducers own disjoint digest shards, and pure-carry shards copy parent run references with zero run I/O.

For a folding round, the implemented GC cost includes one full LIST of `cas/ns/stream/`, one LIST of `gc/server-roots/` plus one mount GET per mount, one HEAD per newly condemned blob, one DELETE per graduate, and one `gc/state` CAS.
`gc_snap_generations_to_keep` defaults to 3; setting it to 0 keeps all generations for forensics.
`ca-gc-dryrun` is read-only and write-free, can over-report away from quiescence because it does not fold new owner events, and its output must never drive a real delete.

A CAS read resolves a ref, reads a manifest, locates an entry, and either decodes inline bytes or performs a ranged GET over the blob payload; inline entries require no additional object-store operation.
Unknown content-addressed disk settings are rejected; `gc_enabled` defaults to `true`, `gc_interval_sec` defaults to 60 seconds, and `gc_shards` defaults to 1.
The CAS verification corpus includes 101 gtest files, 23 TLA+ models, 14 adversarial scenarios, and 51 stateless tests referencing `content_addressed`.

The known CAS gaps include incomplete-list trust in the ref lane, relink dangle risk under incomplete listing, non-atomic `RENAME TABLE`, generation-prune handoff dependence, five adopted-seal GETs per folding round, no within-round manifest cache, and one deliberately open decommission race.

The walkthrough records that older documentation describing mutable `RefSidecar`, a five-phase GC round, binary `CABL`/`CATR` envelopes, protobuf manifests, root shards, or a `mutable_files` sidecar has drifted from the current implementation.
The D1 implementation plan replaces `gc/registry` discovery with `LIST(cas/refs/)` and reclaims empty ref-shard objects so `dropNamespace` no longer leaks a monotone registry and empty shard objects.

The planned shard incarnation is the existing `(writer_epoch, build_sequence)` pair, represented as `ShardIncarnation`, with `{0,0}` meaning unstamped; a recreated `(ns, shard)` must receive a strictly greater pair under `INC-MONO`.
The D1 plan treats read-your-writes enumeration from `LIST(cas/refs/)` as load-bearing; a backend without that consistency is unsupported and must fail closed.
The D1 plan requires new GC fold and discovery tests to run with both `gc_shards=1` and `gc_shards>1`.
The planned `mutateShard` birth path stamps `RootShard::incarnation` only when creating a fresh object and leaves the incarnation immutable when mutating an existing object.

The planned incarnation-aware fold treats a sealed/live incarnation mismatch as an absent prior cursor, restarts at `folded_cursor = 0`, drops carried edges from the old incarnation, and stamps the live incarnation into the new seal.
The planned registry-free newborn protocol creates a precommit-state shard fenced to the current `gcRound`, and gates `promote` on the shard's own `fence_round` rather than a registry fence.
The planned ref-shard reclaim condition is empty refs, a last journal tombstone, complete folding past the fence at the current incarnation, and token-guarded `deleteExact`.
The planned ref-shard reclaim is fail-closed on a concurrent revive: an append changes the token, `deleteExact` returns `TokenMismatch`, and the shard survives with its new content.
The D1 plan makes rerunning the `CaBuildRootPrecommit` TLA+ model mandatory if `Build::precommitAdd` or `Build::promote` changes.

The D1 design is partly superseded: registry removal and `LIST(cas/refs/)` discovery landed as D1, while the `RootShard` incarnation, incarnation-keyed cursor, and newborn-root-shard portions became moot after replacing the mutable root-shard model with per-table snapshot-plus-log state.

The D1 phase-0 model checked `INV_NO_DANGLING` and `INV_NO_ORPHAN_EDGE` across 724,944 distinct states, and its result was that `THM-NO-RETURN` holds without the registry; three sabotage controls demonstrated the need for the newborn floor, incarnation cursor, and fold-before-reclaim ordering.

D1 originated because `dropNamespace` tombstoned shard contents but never removed the namespace from `gc/registry`, causing registry entries and empty ref-shard objects to accumulate as the S30 `other` residual.

Before D1, `discoverUniverse` enumerated `registry.namespaces × shardsToVisit`, so GC fencing cost was proportional to namespaces ever created times `root_shards` and could mint fence-only manifests for absent shards.

Writer deregistration at `dropNamespace` was rejected because removal events carry the blob `-1` edges and removing the namespace from discovery before GC folds them could cause phantom in-degree leaks.
GC deregistration based on an empty settled namespace was rejected because a freshly created live table with no inserts is indistinguishable from a dropped table by emptiness alone.

Deleting and recreating `cas/refs/<ns>/<shard>` under the old path-keyed cursor creates an ABA hazard: a stale `folded_cursor` can skip journal versions 1 through K in the recreated shard, losing its edges.

The D1 design collapses the prior fence coordinates into two orthogonal coordinates: immutable shard `incarnation` for identity and birth ordering, plus pool-global GC `round` for the writer retire-view floor.
The D1 fold cursor is keyed by `(ns, shard, incarnation)`, so a recreated shard with a strictly greater incarnation cannot match an old sealed cursor and is folded from zero.

`RootShard::incarnation` is stamped once at create-if-absent, never mutated by later writes, and is encoded in the root-shard protobuf; missing incarnation data where required is fail-closed because CA has no compatibility scaffolding.

D1 makes `LIST(cas/refs/)` the discovery authority, retains ambiguity detection across pages as a fail-closed condition, and removes `gc/registry`, `RootsRegistry`, `rootsRegistryKey`, `ensureRegistered`, the registry-fence sub-step, and the `_registry` cursor branch.
Under D1, `listNamespaces` is derived from a LIST of `cas/refs/` and is unioned with `roots/` for namespaces containing only verbatim files.
D1 requires strongly consistent LIST with read-your-writes enumeration; S3 is stated to provide it, while an unsupported backend must be documented and fail closed rather than use a silent fallback.

A first publish into a new namespace uses the existing precommit machinery: the ref-shard becomes a precommit-state object, its `+1` is protected by the fold barrier, and there is no separate `pending-newborns` object.
An abandoned newborn is treated as an abandoned precommit and reclaimed by the existing `(writer_epoch, build_sequence)` watermark path; after it empties, tombstone reclaim handles its shard object.

`dropNamespace` appends an explicit tombstone as the last journal event after ref removals, and GC deletes the shard only when it is empty, tombstoned, and folded past a completed fence using `deleteExact(rootShardKey(ns, shard), token)`.
A revive append after a shard tombstone changes the object token, so `deleteExact` returns `TokenMismatch` and the shard survives; an idle-but-live empty shard without a tombstone is retained.
After registry removal, GC fences only discovered shards from `LIST(cas/refs/)`; an absent shard is not minted or fenced, and create ordering is supplied by the precommit gate.
D1 requires `THM-NO-RETURN`, `INV-NO-DANGLING`, `INV-NO-ABA`, and `INV-NO-BLOB-LEAK`; the last requires every `-1` edge to be folded before its carrying shard is deleted.
The D1 design excludes the `/trees/` scaffolding, O(buffer) run-file streaming debt, D2 scenario-threshold triage, and the broad existing-fold sharded test from its implementation scope.
The D1 open risk is that if `(writer_epoch, build_sequence)` does not strictly increase on every recreate, implementation must use a sticky per-`server_root` incarnation allocator instead.
The D1 design treats LIST consistency as load-bearing and requires RustFS and `InMemoryBackend` semantics to be confirmed; an unsupported backend must remain fail-closed.
The condemned-evidence copy-forward proposal is approved and explicitly constrained to the CA layer; it makes no `ReplicatedMergeTree` changes.

A replica restart could remain permanently readonly when a CA part was committed but ZK-unknown, `republishRef` adopted a blob whose token was condemned in a fresh retire view, and `promote` aborted without an attach retry.
All `adoptEvidence` dependencies originate from a committed manifest and therefore represent reference transfer from a currently reachable object, not resurrection of garbage.
Copy-forward rejects recreating from writer-local files because a CA part's files are the pool blobs and no independent source exists on the move path.
A same-`ManifestId` owner-move rename with Δ=0 was rejected because cross-shard moves would create two-owner or zero-owner windows that the source-edge set model cannot represent.
Relaxing the condemned-token gate for non-pending entries was rejected because `SabotageAdoptRetiredToken` demonstrates that binding a listed token is unsafe.

For tokenless evidence dependencies, `observeAndAdmit` reads and verifies the condemned object, wraps the payload with a fresh `incarnation_tag` and this build's `build_id`, and conditionally overwrites the observed token before admitting the new token.

Copy-forward verification requires a valid envelope, matching object kind, and recomputed logical hash equal to the key hash; any mismatch or 404 is fail-closed, with corruption reported as `CORRUPTED_DATA` and a lost-race 404 as `ABORTED`.
A copy-forward overwrite uses `putOverwrite(key, bytes, expected = observed token)`; `PreconditionFailed` triggers a HEAD and bounded re-evaluation, while eight failed attempts end in `ABORTED`.

Successful copy-forward emits `CasEventType::BlobCopyForward` and increments `CasBlobCopyForward`; the old `(hash, t)` entry remains listed until exact-token settlement, while the new incarnation is protected from wrong-token deletion.

The amended resurrection invariant permits reading a condemned object only for verified copy-forward when a live committed manifest supplies `adoptEvidence`; it forbids blind PUT and `putIfAbsent` after a lost delete race.

`CaGcAckFloorCore` models copy-forward as minting and binding a fresh incarnation only while the blob is present and the current token is visible in the writer's loaded retired view; there is no absent-source copy-forward arm.
The implementation notes corrected the corruption outcome: a corrupt copy-forward payload throws `CORRUPTED_DATA`, while a 404 or lost race remains `ABORTED`.

The alleged abandoned copy-forward orphan exists only in a raw `putOverwrite` shape; in the real `republishRef` flow, `stageManifest` and `precommitAdd` precede promote, and the watermark plus fresh-token lifecycle self-heals a writer that dies after the copy-forward PUT.

The copy-forward observability work also records `retired_view_advance` per-view events, `mount_remount` events, and GC round columns `entries_condemned`, `entries_graduated`, `entries_redeleted`, `fence_outs`, `min_ack`, and `anomalies`.
The `FreshEvidenceDepWithViewHitIsResolvedByGate` test's post-fix meaning is promote success through displacement, with the condemned listed token never bound, rather than an `ABORTED` result.

The documentation-consolidation plan requires a small structured `docs/superpowers/cas/` set that captures load-bearing invariants, decisions, failed paths, and technical details without narrative noise.

Every technical claim in the consolidated documentation must be traceable to an old document or the code, and each target document must label relevant sections `DONE`, `TODO`, `REJECTED`, or `DESIRABLE`.

The planned canonical CAS documentation set includes `README.md`, `01-architecture.md` through `08-testing-and-soak.md`, and `ROADMAP.md`, with topic-structured rather than dated or milestone-structured documents.

The consolidation keeps all `docs/superpowers/models/*.tla` and `*.cfg` sources untouched and also keeps the active D1 spec, plan, and model; their prose results and readmes may be consolidated separately.

The consolidation target explicitly assigns GC protocol documentation to cover lease/election, rounds, orphan and ref removal, shard reclaim, incarnation, registry removal, attempt-scoped generations, TLA+ references, and S3 budget links.
No obsolete document may be deleted until a coverage matrix maps it to a canonical section and a fresh sanity audit confirms that its load-bearing content is present.
The consolidation is explicitly synthesis rather than concatenation: new documents should remain manageable, and claims must not be invented.
The ack-floor GC redesign replaces O(universe) per-round fence and recheck phases with a merged per-server heartbeat, a current retired list, and a one-pass three-cursor merge.

An ack-floor entry graduates only when `condemn_round < min_ack`, where `min_ack` is the minimum `observed_gc_round` among live or expired-but-not-fenced heartbeats; terminated and fenced heartbeats are excluded.
A writer advertises `observed_gc_round` only after every in-flight `mutateShard` started under the older view has received its CAS response.

The ack-floor open ordering is claim heartbeat → load `gc/state` and the retired list → stamp the acknowledgement → enable mutations, and retired-list objects must be durable before the `gc/state` CAS publishes the round.
The ack-floor redesign rejects old schema versions fail-closed: schema versions are bumped, malformed data yields `CORRUPTED_DATA`, and future versions yield `NOT_IMPLEMENTED`.
The merged heartbeat extends `MountLease` with `min_active`, `observed_gc_round`, and terminal `gc_fenced`; `UINT64_MAX` is the retired sentinel for `min_active`.
`MountLeaseKeeper::terminate` stamps `expires_at_ms = now` and `min_active = UINT64_MAX`, merging the former watermark farewell into mount release.

`Store::refreshViewForBeat` loads `gc/state` and retired-list objects before swapping the view under an exclusive `view_gate`; any read failure leaves the current round unchanged so the acknowledgement cannot advance.

The writer beat holds a shared `view_gate` lock across the entire `mutateShard` operation, and `Store::open` loads the retire view before starting the keeper so the first heartbeat acknowledges the loaded round.

The current retired-list design adds `RetiredEntry::condemn_round`, adds `GcState::retired_refs`, uses `cas_gc_state` version 4, rejects v3 fail-closed, and has `RetireView::refresh` GET `gc/state` followed by each referenced retired-list object without LIST.

The heartbeat floor excludes terminated mounts using `min_active == UINT64_MAX`, fences expired-unfenced mounts with token-guarded overwrite, and re-reads on a fence-out precondition failure before classifying the entry.

The three-cursor merge graduates entries with `condemn_round < min_ack`, keeps entries at `condemn_round == min_ack`, spares entries whose in-degree recovers, captures a token for new zero-in-degree condemnations, and skips absent blobs.

The planned one-pass ack-floor round computes the heartbeat floor before discovery, folds and merges deltas, deletes graduated entries by exact token, writes retired-list objects, and then performs one `gc/state` CAS; `fence` and `recheck` are removed.
The planned GC skew margin defaults to `mount_lease_ttl_ms / 2` and comes from pool configuration without introducing a new user setting.
The ack-floor redesign moves the mount-fence deadline to `CLOCK_BOOTTIME` because `CLOCK_MONOTONIC` does not advance during VM suspend.

The planned ack-floor observability adds `CasGcRetiredGraduated`, `CasGcRetiredSpared`, `CasGcRetiredCondemned`, `CasGcHeartbeatFenceOuts`, and `CasGcFloorHeldByStaleAck` counters, plus `RoundReport` fields for graduated, spared, condemned, fence-outs, and `min_ack`.
